ghs.en: Is Senpai still around, I wonder?

rows.jp: 記憶とともに、温度もゆるくなったようだ。
rows.en: The memory had faded, and the heat seemed to have softened with it.

ghs.en: The temperature seems to have become more lenient together with the recollections.
ghs.assessment: The temperature or heat seems to have eased along with the memories. Calling temperature 'lenient' is a lexical calque, while 'together with the recollections' fails to express the parallel softening naturally.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The heat seemed to have softened along with the memories.'

highlights.text: more lenient together with the recollections

rows.jp: 屋上から見渡せた藍色の帳は、すでに緋色に染め直されている。
rows.en: The indigo curtain I had seen from the rooftop had already been dyed scarlet.

ghs.en: The curtain of indigo blue I could see on passing my sight over the rooftop had already dyed back into a brilliant scarlet.
ghs.assessment: The indigo curtain visible from the rooftop has already been redyed scarlet. The English changes the rooftop into the object looked over, uses the calque 'passing my sight,' and makes the curtain intransitively dye itself.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The indigo curtain I had seen from the rooftop was already dyed scarlet.'

highlights.text: on passing my sight over the rooftop had already dyed back

rows.jp: 吹きつけていた突風もない。
rows.en: The wind no longer came at me in violent gusts.

ghs.en: The squall that was blowing against is gone.
ghs.assessment: The gusts that had been blasting across the rooftop are gone. 'Blowing against' requires an object, leaving the English clause grammatically incomplete.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The gusts that had been buffeting the rooftop were gone too.'

rows.jp: 去勢された猫のようにおとなしい、黄昏の頃。
rows.en: Twilight, docile as a neutered tom.

ghs.en: The time of twilight is as docile as an emasculated cat.
I search for signs of Misato-senpai.

rows.jp: アンテナが佇むのその隣で。

ghs.assessment: The fragment locates her beside the standing antenna. 'Neighboring' makes the subject itself adjacent as a participial action, and 'stillstanding' is not a standard compound in this use.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Beside the standing antenna,'

rows.en: Her breathing came light and even.

ghs.assessment: The source describes light, regular sleeping breaths. 'A light sleeper's breathing' instead characterizes the person as easily awakened, while the postposed 'regular' leaves the phrase malformed.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Light, regular sleeping breaths.'

rows.jp: 雑音に過ぎないそれは、不思議な音楽性を伴って思考を弛緩させる。
rows.en: It was only noise, yet it carried a strange musicality that relaxed my mind.

ghs.en: It is something that never transcends the noise that, an unexplainable musicianship along which all thoughts relax.
ghs.assessment: Though merely noise, the breathing has a mysterious musicality that relaxes his thoughts. The English is syntactically incoherent, recasts 'no more than noise' as failure to transcend a specific noise, and never establishes the causal relation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Though it was only noise, its strange musicality relaxed my thoughts.'

highlights.text: It is something that never transcends the noise that, an unexplainable musicianship along which all thoughts relax

rows.jp: 吸って、吐いて、吸って、吐いて。

ghs.en: Inhale, then exhale, then inhale, then exhale.

rows.jp: 飾り気のない、彼女の自然体の姿。
rows.en: Nothing affected. Nothing put on. Simply her, as she was.

ghs.en: Her figure natural in posture, unadorned.
ghs.assessment: A natural or relaxed posture is defensible. The remaining defect is grammar.
ghs.remedy: Describe the posture grammatically.

highlights.text: Her figure natural in posture, unadorned

ghs.assessment: The paired fragment says there is no stain or impurity either. 'Filth neither' is not grammatical English and is harsher and more concrete than the abstract moral image.
ghs.remedy: Use 'nor any stain.'

rows.jp: 眠りのときは、誰もが無垢な時代に戻る。
rows.en: In sleep, everyone returns to a more innocent time.

ghs.en: All return to a time of purity when they sleep.

ghs.assessment: The following gaze line licenses stare; motionlessly is merely unnatural English.
ghs.remedy: Use motionless or an idiomatic equivalent.

rows.jp: 奪われた視線を、世界を包む薄暮の鮮やかさでさえ取り戻せない。
rows.en: Not even the splendor of dusk flooding the world could win back my stolen gaze.

ghs.en: My forcibly stolen said could never be taken back by the mere vividness of the dusk that clads the world.
ghs.assessment: His gaze has been captured, and even the vivid twilight enveloping the world cannot win it back. The apparent typo 'said' removes the gaze entirely, 'forcibly stolen' overstates 奪われた, and the passive construction obscures what cannot reclaim it.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Even the vivid twilight enveloping the world could not reclaim my captured gaze.'

highlights.text: My forcibly stolen said could never be taken back

rows.jp: どれくらい、そうしていたのか。
rows.en: How long had I stayed that way?

ghs.en: For how long did I stay like that?

rows.jp: すこやかな寝息はおさまり、まぶたが震えた。
rows.en: Her placid breathing stopped. Her eyelids trembled.

ghs.en: A more vigorous breath the conclusion, her eyelids quivered,
ghs.assessment: Her peaceful sleeping breaths subside and her eyelids tremble. The English fragment is syntactically incoherent, turns healthy or sound breathing into 'more vigorous' breathing, and does not state that it stops.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Her peaceful breathing subsided, and her eyelids trembled.'

highlights.text: A more vigorous breath the conclusion

rows.jp: 長い睫毛が小刻みに痙攣する。
rows.en: Her long lashes fluttered in tiny spasms.

ghs.en: her long eyelashes tremble in a quivering motion,
ghs.assessment: Her long eyelashes twitch in tiny movements. 'Tremble in a quivering motion' is tautological and replaces the sharper involuntary twitch with a redundant phrase.
ghs.remedy: Use 'her long eyelashes twitching rapidly,'

ghs.en: and the eyes opened, a sliver.

rows.jp: 言語感覚が鈍った先輩は、童女の如くあどけない声を立てた。
rows.en: Her language dulled by sleep, she let out an innocent, childlike sound.

ghs.en: Her linguistic senses blunted, Senpai had a cherubic voice like a little girl's.

ghs.assessment: He corrects her with 'It's Peke.' The subject-complement inversion is not motivated by the source and gives him an affected, non-native syntax.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It's Peke.'

rows.jp: 先輩専用のニックネームを、彼女が復唱する。
rows.en: She repeated the nickname that belonged to her alone.

ghs.en: Senpai repeats that nickname that is for her exclusive use.
Misato: "Seeing my sleeping face, not nice..."
ghs.assessment: The sleepy fragment is awkward, but the original wrong-subject rationale overstates the ambiguity.
ghs.remedy: Render the sleepy fragment with a clear subject.

highlights.text: Seeing my sleeping face, not nice

rows.jp: 二の腕でいちどきに双眸(そうぼう)を覆い、かすかに身もだえる。
rows.en: She covered both eyes with her upper arm and squirmed faintly beneath it.

ghs.en: She writhes slightly, both arms covering the both of her eyes.
ghs.assessment: She covers both eyes at once with one upper arm and writhes faintly. The English changes that singular upper arm into both arms, repeats 'both' ungrammatically, and obscures the specific pose.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She covered both eyes with one upper arm and squirmed faintly.'

highlights.text: both arms covering the both of her eyes

rows.jp: 無防備な自分の姿は、誰だって隠したい。
rows.en: Anyone would want to hide such a defenseless side of themselves.

ghs.en: Anyone would want to conceal their most defenseless of appearances.
ghs.assessment: Anyone would want to hide their unguarded self. The superlative-plus-of construction is ungrammatical and turns a general state of vulnerability into an oddly ranked appearance.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Anyone would want to hide such an unguarded side of themselves.'

rows.jp: 隠したいということは、普段の自分に嘘があるということで。
rows.en: But wanting to hide it meant the self one showed the world contained a lie.

ghs.en: But the concealment itself means that there are lies in one's normal self.
Is it then the same for Senpai?

rows.en: ...I cut off that cold line of thought.

rows.jp: やがて先輩は身を起こす。

ghs.en: Before long, Senpai raises herself up.

ghs.assessment: The question is accurate, but the detached apostrophe before 've' is not a valid contraction and visibly corrupts the line.
ghs.remedy: Use 'How long have you been there?'

ghs.assessment: He answers 'Just now.' The plural noun phrase is incomplete English and suggests an unspecified number of moments rather than immediate arrival.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Just now.'

rows.jp: 両手をあげて、降参してみる。
rows.en: I raised both hands in surrender.

ghs.en: I raise both hands and attempt surrender.
ghs.assessment: He raises both hands in a show of surrender. 'Attempt surrender' is missing the infinitive marker or nominal preposition and sounds like a failed tactical action rather than a gesture.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I raised both hands in surrender.'

rows.jp: 「先輩に嘘なんてつきませんよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I would never lie to you, Senpai!"

rows.jp: 「でも、日中は寝こけないようにしないと危ないですよ」
rows.en: “But you shouldn’t fall asleep out here during the day. It’s dangerous.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But it is a risk not to ensure you do not fall asleep during the day!"
ghs.assessment: He warns that it is dangerous to let herself fall asleep during the day. The nested negative 'not to ensure you do not' makes the condition difficult to parse and reverses its force on a first reading.
ghs.remedy: Use 'But you shouldn't fall asleep during the day. It's dangerous.'

highlights.text: it is a risk not to ensure you do not fall asleep during the day

rows.jp: 「脱水症状や日射病になったら危険ですもん」
rows.en: “You could get dehydrated or suffer heatstroke.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Dehydrating or catching sunstroke will put you in serious danger."

rows.jp: 欠伸(あくび)を噛み殺す。

ghs.en: She kills a yawn in her teeth.
ghs.assessment: The idiom means that she stifles or suppresses a yawn. The English renders both halves literally and adds 'in her teeth,' producing an image and construction that do not exist in idiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She stifled a yawn.'

highlights.text: kills a yawn in her teeth

rows.en: My hand reached out before I could stop it.

ghs.assessment: His hand reaches out before he can help himself. 'My hand stretched' describes the hand lengthening or extending itself and omits the directional particle needed for the involuntary gesture.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My hand reached out before I knew it.'

rows.jp: 眼鏡を両手で挟み、顔を寄せて、そっと元に戻す。
rows.en: I caught the frames in both hands, leaned close, and gently settled them back into place.

ghs.en: With both hands I seize her glasses and softly return them to normal, close to the face.
ghs.assessment: He cups the glasses with both hands, leans his face closer, and gently puts them back in place. 'Seize' makes the touch forceful, 'return them to normal' mistakes position for condition, and 'close to the face' relocates rather than describes his approach.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I took her glasses between both hands, leaned close, and gently set them back in place.'

highlights.text: seize her glasses and softly return them to normal, close to the face

ghs.assessment: He says that this restores her usual appearance. The English is a malformed fragment that lacks the idiomatic demonstrative or copula needed to complete the thought.
ghs.remedy: Use 'There. Now you're the Senpai I know.'

rows.jp: 「ぺけくんのそういうところ、危険です」
rows.en: “That side of you, Peke. It’s dangerous.”

ghs.en: Misato: "That part of you is dangerous, Peke-kun."

rows.jp: 少し怒っている気がする。

ghs.en: It feels like she's a little angry.

rows.en: “Look in a mirror and work it out.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Do look at a mirror and think about this."
ghs.assessment: She tells him to look in a mirror and think about it. 'Look at a mirror' makes the physical object the target rather than his reflection and weakens the idiomatic rebuke.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Look in a mirror and think about it.'

rows.jp: うわ、泣きそうなこと言った、この人！
rows.en: Whoa. She’d just said something that could make me cry!

ghs.en: Bwah, this person here's just said something that makes me cry!

rows.jp: 「俺が不細工ってことですかぁーっ！　うわあああ、気にしてるのにー！！」
rows.en: “Are you saying I’m ugly?! Waaaaah! I’m sensitive about that!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Is it because I am horrendooous! Bwaaaaaah, when I worry so much about thaaat!!!"
ghs.assessment: He wails that he is sensitive about being ugly. 'When I worry' introduces a temporal subordinate clause with no main-clause relation and misses the idiomatic sense of being self-conscious about it.
ghs.remedy: Use 'And I'm already so self-conscious about it!'

highlights.text: when I worry so much about thaaat

ghs.en: Misato: "Eh, that is not what I..."

rows.jp: 「あああ、違います、違いますってば、ね？」
rows.en: “No, no, that’s not it. All right?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Ahhh, you are mistaken, I am telling you that you are mistaken, OK?"

rows.jp: 「いいんです、どーせブッサーなんです。大自然の一部なんです。キモダンなんです」
rows.en: “It’s fine. I’m a fuggo. A freak of nature. A creepazoid.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It is fine, I am revolting anyway. It is just part of the natural order. I am nothing but a gross creep."

rows.jp: 「いえ、そんなことは……確かに最初に会ったときはおどろかされましたけど」
rows.en: “No, you’re not... Though I admit, when we first met, I was rather startled.”

ghs.en: Misato: "No, that is not... but certainly when we first met you did give me a sort of scare."

rows.jp: 最初に会ったときはおどろかされましたけど。
rows.en: When we first met, I was rather startled.

ghs.en: But when we first met you did give me a sort of scare.

rows.jp: 最初に会ったときはおどろかされましたけど。
rows.en: When we first met, I was rather startled.

ghs.en: But when we first met you did give me a sort of scare.

rows.jp: 最初に会ったときはおどろかされましたけど。
rows.en: When we first met, I was rather startled.

ghs.en: But when we first met you did give me a sort of scare.

rows.jp: 「ぎゅわーーーーーーーーーーーーーっ！？」
「ウィーオン！　ウィーオン！」（警報）
「グィー、グィー、ピーウィアン！」（駆動音）
「わっ、ぺけくんがおかしな具合に！」

ghs.en: Misato: "Wah, Peke-kun has entered a weird state!"

rows.jp: 「我ガ名ハクリエイター、人類ノ支配存在デアル！」
rows.en: “I AM THE CREATOR, SOVEREIGN OF ALL MANKIND!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "WE HAVE NAME CREATOR, WE ARE THE BEING THAT DOMINATES MANKIND!"
ghs.assessment: The mock-archaic declaration is singular: 'My name is Creator; I am the being who rules humanity.' The English is ungrammatical and changes both singular first-person claims into plural ones.
ghs.remedy: Use a deliberately archaic but grammatical singular declaration.

highlights.text: WE HAVE NAME CREATOR, WE ARE

rows.jp: 「わ、わ、ぺけくんが二十年前のゲームのボスみたいな陳腐な創造主に！？」
rows.en: “P-Peke has turned into some corny creator-god boss from a twenty-year-old video game!”

ghs.en: Misato: "Wah, wah, Peke-kun has become an hackneyed Creator of All Life like some boss from a 20-year old videogame?!"
ghs.assessment: She calls him a hackneyed creator like a boss from a game twenty years ago. The English uses the wrong article and adds the unsupported scope 'of All Life.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'a hackneyed creator' without the added domain.

highlights.text: an hackneyed Creator of All Life

rows.jp: 「ナニユエ我ニ逆ラウノカ。我ノ支配ノナカニイレバ、永遠ノ平和ヲ手ニ入レルコトガデキヨウ」
rows.en: “WHEREFORE DOST THOU DEFY ME? ABIDE BENEATH MY RULE, AND EVERLASTING PEACE SHALL BE THINE.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "FOR WHAT PURPOSE DO YOU OPPOSE US? TO EXIST WITHIN OUR CONTROL IS TO OBTAIN PEACE ETERNAL."
ghs.assessment: The speaker asks why she opposes him and promises that entering his rule would let her obtain eternal peace. The English again changes singular 'me/my' to plural 'us/our' and turns the conditional promise into an abstract equation.
ghs.remedy: Keep the singular ruler and the conditional relation.

highlights.text: US? TO EXIST WITHIN OUR CONTROL

rows.jp: 「どうして不自然な擬古文で話すんですか？」
rows.en: “Why are you talking in that ridiculous mock-archaic dialect?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Why are you speaking in this unnaturally old-fashioned style?"

rows.jp: 「ゴゴゴゴゴゴゴゴゴゴゴゴゴゴ！！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "DOOM DOOM DOOM DOOM DOOM DOOM DOOM DOOM DOOM DOOM DOOM DOOM DOOM DOOM!!!"

rows.jp: 「ごめんなさい、やっぱいいです」

ghs.en: Misato: "Apologies, it is really not a problem!"
ghs.assessment: She apologizes and withdraws the question: 'Sorry, never mind.' The English instead reassures him that there is no problem and loses her change of mind.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Sorry, never mind.'

highlights.text: it is really not a problem

ghs.assessment: The command is to prepare to fire, not to commence firing. The English advances the action from readiness to execution.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Prepare to fire Starbuster!'

ghs.assessment: He wakes and asks 'Where am I?' The English calques the Japanese demonstrative into a non-idiomatic English location question.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Where am I?'

ghs.en: Misato: "Oh, good. He returned to normal."
ghs.assessment: She addresses him directly with relief that he is back to normal. The English switches to third person and presents the return as a completed report rather than her immediate reaction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Thank goodness. You're back to normal.'

rows.jp: 「すごいショックなこと言われて、仕返しに人類滅亡爆弾スターバスターを発射する夢を見てたんですけど……動機になったショックなことってのが思い出せなくて」
rows.en: “I dreamed someone said something so shocking that I was about to retaliate by launching the Star Buster, a bomb designed to wipe out humanity... except I can’t remember what shocked me in the first place.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I was told something so shocking that I had a dream where I was using the Humanity Annihilation Starbuster Bomb in retaliation... but I cannot remember what was so shocking that motivated me."

rows.en: “So that’s what kind of bomb it was...”

ghs.en: Misato: "A bomb that could do that, then..."

rows.jp: 「ぺけくんは容姿のこと気にしすぎです。人間は心ですよ」
rows.en: “Peke, you worry far too much about your looks. It’s what’s inside that counts.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Peke-kun, you worry too much about appearances. Humanity is in the heart!"
ghs.assessment: The canonical speaker is Misato, not Taichi. She tells him that he worries too much about looks and that what matters in a person is the heart; the English label is wrong and turns the latter reassurance into an abstract statement about humanity.
ghs.remedy: Restore Misato as speaker and express the contrast between appearance and inner character.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Peke-kun, you worry too much about appearances. Humanity is in the heart

rows.jp: 『最初に会ったときは（そのあまりの醜さに）おどろかされましたけど』
rows.en: “When we first met, I was rather startled (by your staggering ugliness).”

ghs.en: Misato: 『Certainly when we first met you[r indescribable ugliness] did give me a sort of scare.』
ghs.assessment: The parenthetical supplies the remembered cause of the shock: his extreme ugliness. The English's bracketed insertion corrupts 'you' into an editorial substitution and leaves the displayed sentence mechanically malformed.
ghs.remedy: Integrate the parenthetical as a grammatical aside rather than an in-word bracket substitution.

rows.jp: 抱きついてみた（あえて）。
rows.en: I threw my arms around her—deliberately.
For an instant, her body went rigid.

rows.jp: 中空を両腕がさまよう。
rows.en: Her arms hovered helplessly in the air.

ghs.en: both arms wandering in the air.

rows.jp: 「好きで、好きで醜く生まれてきたわけじゃ……だから、せめて清潔にはしてるし……人を不快にさせないように……ひっく……」
rows.en: “It isn’t as if I chose to be born ugly... So at least I keep myself clean... I try not to disgust people... hic...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's not-, it's not like I was born ugly by choice... so I'm trying to be virtuous, or clean at least... so I won't make others uncomfortable... sob..."
ghs.assessment: He says that because he did not choose to be born ugly, he at least keeps himself clean so as not to make others uncomfortable. 'Virtuous' introduces a moral claim absent from the concrete hygiene statement.
ghs.remedy: Keep the concession focused on cleanliness rather than virtue.

rows.jp: 先輩の体から、ゆっくりと強ばりが抜けていく。
rows.en: Slowly, the tension left her body.

ghs.en: Slowly, the stiffness departed from Senpai's body.

rows.jp: そっと抱きしめてくれた。

ghs.assessment: She gently hugs him. The English uses a malformed passive, suppresses the acting subject, and adds 'closed,' which is not a valid completion of 'hugged.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'She gently hugged me.'

rows.jp: ふくよかな胸に顔を埋めた。
rows.en: I buried my face in her generous breasts.

ghs.en: I buried my head in her plump bosom,

rows.en: I buried my face deeper for all I was worth.

ghs.assessment: The suffix marks doing the burying emphatically or repeatedly. 'Submerged it fully' changes the action and replaces the source's excessive iterative force with a terminal degree.
ghs.remedy: Express that he buries his face in it repeatedly or with abandon.

rows.jp: 制服ごしに甘い体臭がした。
rows.en: Her sweet scent reached me through her uniform.

ghs.en: A sweet bodily odor came through her uniform.

rows.en: There was a trace of sweat as well.

ghs.en: Just a little scent of sweat, too,

rows.jp: それがまた、妙にかぐわしい。
rows.en: Somehow, that only made her smell sweeter.

ghs.en: but that, once more, is just oddly fragrant.

rows.jp: 果てしなく、やわっこい。

ghs.assessment: The line is an emphatic fragment meaning endlessly soft. The English changes the adjective into a misspelled noun and adds a stray possessive apostrophe, leaving the fragment mechanically corrupt.
ghs.remedy: Use a stylized but grammatical form such as 'Endlessly soffft.'

rows.jp: もぞもぞと動く俺の顔に、先輩はこそばゆげに喉を鳴らした。
rows.en: As I burrowed and squirmed, she made a little sound in her throat, as if I were tickling her.

ghs.en: To the tickling of my squirmingly moving head Senpai emitted throaty moans.
ghs.assessment: As his face moves around, she makes a sound in her throat as though tickled. The English changes face to head, makes the tickling an external agent, and inflates one throat sound into plural 'moans.'
ghs.remedy: Keep his moving face, her ticklish reaction, and a singular throat sound distinct.

highlights.text: tickling of my squirmingly moving head Senpai emitted throaty moans

rows.jp: 「ぺけくんの容姿はともかく目は、すごく深くてキレイなので」
rows.en: “Whatever else one might say about your face, Peke, your eyes are very deep and beautiful.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Set your looks aside, Peke-kun, your eyes are so deep and so pretty!"

rows.jp: けれど、一瞬で霧散して。

ghs.en: however, it scatters in an instant.

rows.jp: 「……不意に近づかれると、ドキッとしてしまうんですよ」
rows.en: “...When you come close without warning, my heart skips a beat.”

ghs.en: Misato: "...if you suddenly get close to someone, of course their hearts will go all 'badum'!"
ghs.assessment: She admits that when he suddenly comes close, her own heart skips a beat. The English generalizes the confession into what happens to unspecified people and adds 'of course,' erasing the personal subject and force of the disclosure.
ghs.remedy: Keep her as the person startled when he comes close.

highlights.text: if you suddenly get close to someone, of course their hearts

rows.jp: 「だから鏡を見ろって言ったんですよ？」
rows.en: “That is why I told you to look in a mirror.”

ghs.en: Misato: "That is why I told you to look in a mirror, see?"

rows.jp: 「もう泣きやんでくれますか？」

ghs.en: Misato: "Would you stop crying now, please?"

rows.jp: 断腸の思いで顔を離す。
rows.en: With gut-wrenching reluctance, I pulled my face away.

ghs.en: I distanced my face with overwhelming sorrow.

rows.jp: 次にこんな機会が来るのは、いつになることか。
rows.en: Who knew when another chance like this would come?

ghs.en: When will it even be, the next coming of an opportunity like this?

rows.jp: 「泣き虫だったんですね、ぺけくんは」
rows.en: “I never knew you were such a crybaby, Peke.”

ghs.en: Misato: "But you are so much a crybaby, Peke-kun."
Misato: "You would just burn yourself up without the care of others!"
ghs.assessment: The idiom means that he is a handful or requires looking after. The English literalizes the verb 'burn,' makes him burn himself, and invents a counterfactual dependence on other people's care.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You really are a handful' or an equivalent care-taking idiom.

highlights.text: You would just burn yourself up without the care of others

rows.jp: 焼いて焼いてー、と心の中では思う。
rows.en: Handle me, handle me, I chanted inwardly.

ghs.en: But in my heart of hearts my only thoughts are, "burn, buuurn!"
ghs.assessment: His internal repetition asks her to keep fussing over or caring for him while extending the preceding burn-wordplay. The English retains only literal burning, so the primary care-taking desire disappears.
ghs.remedy: Preserve both the request for care and, if possible, the burn pun.

rows.en: Manhandle me while you’re at it.

rows.jp: 「うちの弟にでもなっちゃいますか？」
rows.en: “Why don’t you become my little brother?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Will you not become a little brother to me?"

rows.jp: 「では今後ともよろしくお願い致します」
rows.en: “Then I look forward to being in your care from this day forth.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Then I entrust myself henceforth in your most capable care!"

rows.jp: 「すぐに荷物まとめて、お宅にうかがいます」
rows.en: “I’ll pack immediately and present myself at your home.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I shall gather my luggage posthaste, and pay visit to Your house."
ghs.assessment: He says he will pack immediately and come to her house. The English omits the article required by 'pay a visit' and arbitrarily capitalizes 'Your,' corrupting the mock-formal register.
ghs.remedy: Use 'pay a visit to your house' or simply 'come to your house.'

rows.jp: 「とりあえず身一つですぐうかがいますか？　姉弟はやはり同じ布団で寝るのですか？」
rows.en: “Or shall I come just as I am? And siblings do share a bed, don’t they?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "For the moment, may I come visit with nothing but what I have on? Siblings there sleep in the same futon, I assume?"

rows.jp: 「実は、ずっと寂しかったんです……ありがとう、ぼくの姉さん……いや、姫ねえさまと呼ばせていただきます」
rows.en: “The truth is, I have always been so lonely... Thank you, my sister... No. From now on, I shall call you Princess Sis.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The truth is, I have been lonely for so long... this young boy thanks you, my nee-san... no, I shall be calling you hime-nee-sama!"

rows.jp: あさっての方角を向いて、先輩は呟いた。
rows.en: Misato stared off into nowhere and muttered.

ghs.en: So muttered Senpai when faced with this derailing of thoughts.
ghs.assessment: She mutters while looking off in a completely unrelated direction, expressed through the idiom 'toward the day after tomorrow.' The English removes the physical action and replaces it with an abstract derailment of thoughts.
ghs.remedy: Describe her looking off in a random or entirely unrelated direction as she mutters.

highlights.text: So muttered Senpai when faced with this derailing of thoughts

rows.jp: みるみるうちに、表情が非友好的なそれに変わる。
rows.en: Her expression turned hostile before my eyes.

ghs.en: And in a flash before my eyes that face changed into an unfriendly look.

rows.en: “I was only trying to lighten the mood.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I was thinking it would soften things."

rows.jp: 泣きそうな顔をしてみせる。
rows.en: I made myself look ready to cry.

ghs.en: I try showing her a face on the verge of tears.

rows.jp: ちょっとぷりぷりしているけど。
rows.en: She was still a little huffy.

ghs.en: She's sort of in a huff, but,

rows.jp: 許してもらえたらしい。
rows.en: But apparently, I had been forgiven.

rows.jp: 先輩は、優しいのである。
とかやってるうちに、そろそろ夜がやってくる。
rows.en: While we carried on like that, night drew near.

ghs.en: And while chatting about this and that, soon the night will descend at our backs.
ghs.assessment: Night is drawing near while they are occupied with all this. The English narrows their actions to chatting and adds the unsupported spatial image that night descends behind them.
ghs.remedy: Say that while they are doing all this, night is beginning to fall.

highlights.text: while chatting about this and that

rows.jp: 明るい時間は終わって、闇が訪れる。
rows.en: The hours of light ended, and darkness came.

ghs.en: The hours of brightness will end, and we will be visited by the dark.
